description: Fractional-percent sale fixture: list 100.00 / sale 87.50, an EXACT 12.5% discount
notes: Seeded by seed-standard-products.mjs (seeded=true) from the sale_price column. list 100.00 / sale 87.50 gives a raw discount fraction of EXACTLY 0.1250. VCST-5691 shipped in vc-module-x-api ProductPrice.GetDiscountPercent as Math.Round(fraction, 4, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero) - NOT the IMoneyRoundingPolicy the ticket proposed (a reviewer overrode that during review), so there is no rounding policy to configure. xAPI PriceType.discountPercent must report 0.1250 and never a whole-percent 0.12. Every pre-existing coupon/sale fixture is an integer percent, which cannot detect the defect. Ratio drift-guarded by td:validate:standard check [12] against standard-specs.mjs DISCOUNT_RATIO_FIXTURES. No GUID committed - resolved by SKU.

description: Rounding-midpoint sale fixture: list 200.00 / sale 175.31, a raw discount fraction of exactly 0.12345
notes: Seeded by seed-standard-products.mjs (seeded=true) from the sale_price column. (200.00 - 175.31) / 200.00 = 24.69 / 200.00 = EXACTLY 0.12345, which lands ON the 4-decimal rounding midpoint: MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero gives 0.1235 while bankers/ToEven gives 0.1234. That divergence IS the fixture - a ratio off the midpoint silently proves nothing. Both prices are ordinary 2-decimal money, so the midpoint is genuinely expressible at platform price precision; no exotic 10000.00-scale price is needed. Ratio AND midpoint divergence are drift-guarded by td:validate:standard check [12]. No GUID committed - resolved by SKU.
